Not a mod here, but I don't see anything wrong with that, it's still camping (even though you're cheating!). I know what you're saying though. I'm in my early 30s and while I still do tent camping, sleeping on the ground just isn't as fun as it used to be

Thanks! Maybe now that my kids are grown it might be fun to get back into a tent. Sure is a lot less overhead than when we had two toddlers with us.

I have some thoughts on my favourite spots in Ontario....and have questions on how to try hiking/camping. I'll get some submissions going and hope for some responses!

As someone with kids that are just coming out of the toddler phase, I hear ya. I absolutely do not miss lugging training toilets and diapers, tons and tons of extra clothing and toys and pillows... one day here in the near future I'll be able to convince everyone to stick to a single pack and we'll go backwoods camping.

...in my dreams, there's no toilets in the woods, missus won't hear of it.

A guy I work with took his 3 year old backwoods camping. He said it was tough, but fun. My kids would never have put up with it, but I guess they are all different!

I remember ours screaming at night (hard to get them to sleep in the tent). We ended up packing them into their car seats and drove around the campground until they fell asleep. Poor neighbours.

Tell you what, I've gotten so much more tolerant of other people and their kids since I've been taking mine out. They're older now and don't cry, will fall asleep in the tent etc, but I won't ever so much as complain if I hear some loud, unhappy kids out camping.

I believe it's important to get them out and start them camping quite young. Little kids are going to be fussy and cry, it's outdoors, it's foreign to them. But they'll get better, that's why you're out there right now - getting them better at camping.

I'm excited to think, here in a few years I'll have some actual help setting up the site! That's gonna be some sweet camping.

Mine are actually 20 and 22 now...I was referring to our past experiences. We've taken the kids out since my youngest was 9 months old....and you are correct...mine love to go camping to this day, and we make a point to squeeze it into everyone's schedule a minimum of once per summer. Camp fires and board games and hiking together is a wonderful experience even with my young adults. However, they are a bit wary of the backwoods thing. I'll just be trying it with my husband.

And help setting up the site is awesome! We even convinced them to do all the set up work once when we sat back with a beer. Even better is when they can go to the bathrooms by themselves. :)

Even better is when they can go to the bathrooms by themselves.

I think I look forward to that more than any other single thing I can think of, holy smokes. I sincerely hope I can keep us a camping family past the kids' teen years.
